title: Strict interval attachments represent derived pushouts
statement: Use the Bergner model structure on small simplicial categories and its homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ as in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], and derived pushouts of small spans (ordinary pushouts of cofibrant replacements of the span) as in [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping]. Let $[1]$ be the discrete walking arrow and let $\mathbb J$ be the discrete two-object groupoid with one arrow in each ordered direction. Fix a factorization $[1]\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{r}\mathbb J$ with $i$ a cofibration and $r$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. For every small simplicial category $D$, every small set $V$, and every simplicial functor from $\coprod_{v\in V}[1]$ to $D$ selecting the labelled vertex arrows, put $A=\coprod_{v\in V}[1]$, $B=\coprod_{v\in V}K$, and $P=D\amalg_A B$. The canonical comparison map from the derived pushout of the span $D\leftarrow A\rightarrow B$ to this ordinary pushout $P$ is an isomorphism in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ under $D$. This comparison is natural in maps of such labelled spans, valid for arbitrary $D$, and includes repeated or coincident attaching vertices and the empty set $V$.

source.place: Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Proposition A.3.5.5, printed pp.891--893 (PDF pp.908--910); strict-localization universal property and its ordinary-pushout comparison. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-category theorem.
